A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CMT‐3 is a novel chemopreventative agent that inhibits the invasive potential of cancer cells by inhibiting the expression of MMP‐9 and by inhibiting MMP activity.
CMT-3 inhibits MMP-9 expression, release and activity in a breast cancer cell line.
CMTs can be used to suppress tumour invasion and metastasis, and if used with other chemotherapeutic agents, could lead to more successful treatments for cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

CMT-3 inhibits the ability of tumor cells to invade the surrounding extracellular matrix (a process known as metastasis), and that it does so by reducing levels of MMP-9, a key protein that is required to break down the matrix.
CMT-3 inhibits the release and activity of MMP-9, and thus the degradation of ECM.
the inhibition of MMP-9 by CMT-3 may be useful for preventing breast cancer metastasis.
